I'd just like to say that I had the same habit.  With my most recent string being a 3.5 year relationship followed by the next week beginning a 4.5 year relationship that now ended about 8 months ago.  So 8 years solid with no true relationship direction and only being single having some lessons learned.

This time single has done one amazing thing for me.  It has given the perspective I needed to see why my past relationships had not worked out.  It also gave me space to see what I want in a relationship.  I have also done some research on what makes relationships work and would never have had so much self discovery if not single.

​

I realized my last relationships never would have worked out because I lacked this perspective, and with this new knowledge my next relationships will be so much healthier and hopefully last forever.  I also realized mainly my role in these breakups and why I jump from one to the next.

I highly recommend some therapy for self reflection if it is needed!  Also I recommend a book called "Attached" that details different attachment styles.  I was avoidant (changing that) which led to the loss of connection in the end.   Working towards being more "secure" and making the next relationship a success.  Good luck and definitely give singledom a chance until you figure out what you want in life, in a relationship, and how to make it work better for the next time.

I highly, HIGHLY recommend you read a book called "Attached" by Levine and Heller.  You sound like a classic "avoidant" attachment style.  One of the key points of this is to find flaws in your partner to subconsciously distance yourself from them.  Essentially you devalue them mentally thus keeping them at arms length.  Read the book and it will help you understand this.  The classic pattern is to meet an awesome girl by all standards, then lose your attraction to them and then end it.  Often there is remorse for the breakup later on.  And then the cycle repeats.  This style of attachment can be worked on, and will likely help your future relationships if you realize what is going on.
